exercise.title: Fast runs, rising and falling
exercise.why: Runs in songs fall more often than they rise, and a falling run tends to go flat, so the way down gets its own stages.

cells.text: Press Play below to hear the run: the mic starts with it. It is the nine-note run, as fast on the way up as on the way down: it goes from Do up to Re above the high Do and back, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it on "ah" and close towards "oo" at the top.

cells.heading: The falling run on the click

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below to start the metronome and the mic. From the high {{1}}, sing the run {{1}} {{b7}} {{5}} {{4}} in one beat and land on {{b3}} on the next, then step down to the low {{1}} and hold it. Sing it on "oo".
When {{b3}} lands on the click and in tune, try a faster stage. Use the Stage selector below to change the tempo, then press Start exercise again.
If the low notes of the run sag at a new stage, go back one stage.

cells.heading: The pentatonic run, with the metronome

cells.text: Press Play below to hear the pentatonic run with the metronome under it: the mic starts with it. The run goes from La below Do up to the high Do, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it on "ah", and keep every pass on the beat.
